title: Henselian rigidity for w-contractible lisse condensed sheaves
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $D(T,\Lambda)=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_T)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with ordinary derived tensor and unit $\Lambda_T[0]$, and $D_{\mathrm{lis}}(T,\Lambda)$ for its full subcategory of dualizable objects (objects admitting evaluation and coevaluation satisfying both triangle identities). For a profinite set $S$, use the analogous notation for sheaves on profinite sets over $S$, with finite jointly surjective covering families and coefficient ring the restriction of $\Lambda$ to that site. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, with the closed immersion $i:Z\to T$. Then $\pi_0(Z)\to\pi_0(T)$ is a homeomorphism, and $T$ is w-contractible [sk-def-pe-wlocal] if and only if $Z$ is w-contractible. When these conditions hold, the exact symmetric monoidal inverse image induces an equivalence
$$i^*:D_{\mathrm{lis}}(T,\Lambda)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{\mathrm{lis}}(Z,\Lambda).$$
In particular it is fully faithful on morphisms between dualizable objects. The coefficient identification $i^*\Lambda_T\cong\Lambda_Z$ is the canonical one, so $i^*$ commutes with the scalar extension of constant discrete complexes.

proof.text: Apply the henselian-pair definition [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] to the finite $A$-algebra $A$ itself. It gives a bijection $\operatorname{Idem}(A)\to\operatorname{Idem}(A/I)$. Under [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent], the clopen corresponding to $e$ is $D(e)$, and $i^{-1}D(e)=D(\overline e)$. Thus inverse image is a bijection between the clopens of $T$ and those of $Z$.

source.place: Corollary 4.4(1), proof; Stacks Tag 09XI, more-algebra.tex, lemma-characterize-henselian-pair (3)

proof.text: Put $P=\pi_0(T)$, $Q=\pi_0(Z)$ and $h=\pi_0(i):Q\to P$. By [sk-def-pe-wlocal] the underlying spaces of these affine schemes are spectral; [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite] makes $P,Q$ compact Hausdorff. Every clopen of a space is a union of components, and hence descends to a clopen of its component quotient. Therefore Step 1 says that $h^{-1}$ is a bijection on clopens. The formula of [lem-weil-pbc-quasicompact-components-clopen-intersection], applied to $T$ and $Z$, separates distinct components by clopens. If $q_1\ne q_2$ in $Q$, choose a separating clopen in $Q$ and lift it along $h^{-1}$; this separates $h(q_1),h(q_2)$, proving injectivity. The image $K=h(Q)$ is compact, hence closed in $P$. If $p\notin K$, for each $k\in K$ choose a clopen containing $p$ and excluding $k$. Compactness of $K$ gives finitely many whose intersection $V$ misses $K$. Then $h^{-1}V=\varnothing=h^{-1}\varnothing$, contradicting injectivity on clopens since $p\in V$. So $h$ is surjective. A continuous bijection from compact to Hausdorff is a homeomorphism: it sends closed sets to compact, thus closed, sets.

source.place: Corollary 4.4(1), finite clopen subdivisions argument, written out via component separation

proof.text: By [lem-zl-henselian-wstrict-local-invariance], $A$ is w-strictly local exactly when $A/I$ is. By Step 2, $P$ is extremally disconnected exactly when $Q$ is: a homeomorphism preserves open sets, their closures, and openness of those closures. The definition [sk-def-pe-wlocal] of w-contractibility is the conjunction of these two conditions, so $T$ is w-contractible if and only if $Z$ is.

Assume these equivalent conditions. Apply [lem-zl-condensed-wcontractible-lisse-evaluation] to the two w-contractible affine schemes $T$ and $Z$. The coefficient-compatible component maps give equivalences $\pi_T^*:D_{\mathrm{lis}}(P,\Lambda)\simeq D_{\mathrm{lis}}(T,\Lambda)$ and $\pi_Z^*:D_{\mathrm{lis}}(Q,\Lambda)\simeq D_{\mathrm{lis}}(Z,\Lambda)$. Also [lem-zl-condensed-lisse-proetale-locality], for the scheme morphism $i$, gives the exact symmetric monoidal functor $i^*$, its restriction to dualizable objects, and its canonical coefficient identification.

The square of component maps commutes with $i$ and $h$. Here this includes the maps of sites, not only the point maps: the component-site construction in [lem-zl-condensed-wcontractible-lisse-evaluation] starts with finite clopen subdivisions. A clopen $U\subseteq P$ gives the open-and-closed part $T_U\subseteq T$; pulling back gives $Z\times_TT_U=Z_{h^{-1}U}$. Thus the two composite constructions agree on every finite subdivision and on their inverse-limit construction of a profinite set over $P$. Functoriality of inverse image gives $i^*\pi_T^*\cong\pi_Z^*h^*$, compatibly with coefficients, since each coefficient ring is pulled back from the same condensed ring $\Lambda$.

source.place: Corollary 4.4(2), final sentence, with the construction (4.1) preceding Proposition 4.3

proof.text: Since $h$ is a homeomorphism, relabelling profinite sets over $P$ by $h$ gives an inverse to $h^*$, also on the dualizable subcategories. By Steps 4 and 5, $i^*$ is conjugate by $\pi_T^*,\pi_Z^*$ to this equivalence. Hence $i^*$ is an equivalence and in particular gives bijections on all morphism sets between dualizable objects. Finally [lem-zl-condensed-lisse-proetale-locality] identifies $i^*(\Lambda_T\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline C)$ with $\Lambda_Z\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline C$ for every constant discrete scalar complex $C\in D(R)$, $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$; this is the required canonical scalar-extension compatibility.

source.place: Corollary 4.4(2), conclusion; Section 3 pullback paragraph before (3.1)
